chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudaylah, from Aban, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
"The prayer of the two Eids is only for the resident, and there is no prayer except with an Imam."

key_terms.الْمُقِيمِ: The resident (one who is not traveling)
key_terms.صَلاَةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: The prayer of the two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the validity of Eid prayers regarding residency and leadership?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies that Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha prayers are obligatory for residents (muqim) and explicitly conditions their validity on the presence of an Imam, reflecting the Shia view of the Imam's central role in public worship. It underscores the communal and hierarchical nature of these prayers, distinguishing them from individual acts of devotion. The ruling highlights the continuity of Imamate authority in maintaining religious observances.
